body.x: SpeedFloor Co., Ltd. (CEO Hyunjin Hong, Austin Hong) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

SpeedFloor, which provides fully automated logistics solutions, introduced its automated loading and unloading system. This system is designed to enhance operational efficiency at logistics sites while reducing the physical burden on workers. The company emphasized that its efforts extend beyond device development and supply, aiming to achieve full automation by integrating with automated logistics centers.

The automated system has garnered demand from government entities such as Korea's Ministry of National Defense and Incheon Metropolitan City and private companies like Kurly. A SpeedFloor representative stated, "Our solution has been validated to reduce labor loads for logistics workers, ranging from soldiers to delivery drivers. Transport companies have also reported increased profits due to shortened turnaround times. Based on this data, we are planning to expand internationally."

Participating in CES 2025, SpeedFloor sought to identify the specific needs of global businesses and government agencies in preparation for its overseas expansion. The company also aimed to build partnerships and explore new business opportunities through networking with venture capitalists, logistics companies, and tech firms.

The automated loading and unloading system showcased at CES 2025 allows users to move cargo forward and backward inside a truck's cargo space without physically entering it. This is achieved using a conveyor belt-like device operated via simple button controls. The system, which combines chain and belt structures, is supported by 17 patent applications. The integrated chain-belt conveyor and moving partition plate enable seamless transportation of irregularly shaped cargo, including bulk goods, without malfunctions.

body.cap: SpeedFloor introduces its solution to Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter | Photo by AVING News

body.x: This innovative technology has already led to significant achievements, including an initial purchase of one unit by Korea's Ministry of National Defense and an additional 18 units. The representative explained, "Loading and unloading heavy military supplies traditionally requires many personnel, and the risk of injury is high. The Ministry adopted our product to offset reduced manpower and alleviate the workload of soldiers." Furthermore, 17 units have been deployed in Incheon Metropolitan City's logistics digitization project.

SpeedFloor expressed its ambition to realize fully automated logistics. In logistics centers, cargo typically moves through three stages: unloading from large transport vehicles, sorting, and reloading onto smaller delivery vehicles. Currently, all these stages require human intervention. The company emphasized that integrating its solution into warehouses would minimize labor requirements, saving time and costs.

A representative stated, "When large transport vehicles arrive at logistics centers, cargo can be unloaded automatically, sorted using our ongoing research into an automated sorting system, and reloaded onto delivery vehicles without manual intervention. This process will enable fully automated logistics centers. Furthermore, we plan to expand automation by integrating autonomous driving technologies." They concluded, "As logistics demand continues to grow, SpeedFloor's solution is positioned to respond efficiently."
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
